newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Zambia and Kabila's Congo to tackle smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Zambia and Kabila's Congo to tackle smuggling.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia have agreed to work together to improve security along their common border to reduce smuggling.
Zambia's Home Affairs Minister Chitalu Sampa told state television in Kinshasa late on Wednesday that the two neighbours were to harmonize their views on smuggling.

"We met our Congolese counterpart to discuss problems encountered along our common border, (namely) thefts of motor vehicles and thefts of copper," Sampa told the television after talks with Congolese Internal Affairs Minister Mwenze Kongolo.
Both countries are copper-rich. Cars stolen in Zambia are sold in Kabila's Congo at low prices. Many people make a living smuggling copper in and out of the two countries.
"We worked together to harmonize our views and see how we can set a term to this situation," Sampa said.
Kabila toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko after a seven-month war in May. Relations between Zaire and Zambia were not particularly warm under Mobutu.
Zambian President Frederick Chiluba attended Kabila's May inauguration and Kinshasa independence celebrations this week.
